dau-hu-non-sot-nam-dong-co.name: Silken Tofu with Shiitake Mushroom Sauce
dau-hu-non-sot-nam-dong-co.description: Soft steamed silken tofu is topped with a light, gently thickened shiitake sauce. A mild vegetarian option for serving with rice.
dau-hu-non-sot-nam-dong-co.finished_dish: The tofu stays soft and intact; shiitake mushrooms are tender and the savory sauce lightly coats each piece.
dau-hu-non-sot-nam-dong-co.serving: Serve warm with the mushroom sauce spooned over the tofu and steamed rice.
tips: Steam the tofu just until heated so it keeps its shape.
Dissolve the starch in cool water before adding it to the pan.
Choose vegetarian oyster sauce and seasonings for a fully plant-based meal.
dau-hu-non-sot-nam-dong-co.image_alt: Silken tofu topped with shiitake mushroom sauce, scallions, and cilantro.

ingredients.name: Silken tofu
ingredients.notes: Drain and cut into large bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Fresh shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim tough stems, rinse, and slice.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Separate white parts for the sauce and chop the green parts.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop for garnish.

ingredients.name: Sesame oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the scallion whites and mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Choose a product labeled vegetarian.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the product.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in cool water before use.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the sauce and starch slurry.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Add only if the sauce needs more seasoning.

preparation_steps: Drain and cut the tofu into large bite-size pieces. Trim and slice the mushrooms; dissolve the tapioca starch in two tablespoons of cool water.
Rinse the scallions, separate the white parts from the green parts, and chop the cilantro.
cooking_steps: Steam the tofu for about 5–6 minutes until heated through; keep it warm on a serving plate.
Warm the sesame oil, sauté the scallion whites until fragrant, then add the mushrooms and cook until just tender.
Add vegetarian oyster sauce, soy sauce, and water. Simmer gently for 2–3 minutes and taste.
Stir the starch slurry again, add it gradually, and cook until the sauce is lightly thickened. Spoon it over the tofu and finish with scallion greens and cilantro.
dau-hu-non-sot-nam-dong-co.serving_basis: A four-person dish for a Vietnamese family meal.
dau-hu-non-sot-nam-dong-co.time_note: About 30 minutes including preparation, resting, and cooking.

muc-ong-xao-dua-hanh-tay.name: Squid Stir-Fried with Pineapple and Onion
muc-ong-xao-dua-hanh-tay.description: Squid is quickly stir-fried with sweet-tart pineapple and onion, then lightly seasoned with fish sauce. The tender-crisp dish fits a weeknight rice meal.
muc-ong-xao-dua-hanh-tay.finished_dish: The squid is just cooked and tender; pineapple remains in pieces, onion is soft, and a light sauce coats the ingredients.
muc-ong-xao-dua-hanh-tay.serving: Serve immediately while hot with steamed rice.
tips: Drain the squid well before stir-frying to keep the pan from becoming watery.
Cook the squid over high heat and remove it as soon as it firms, then return it near the end.
Add fish sauce gradually because brands vary in saltiness.
search_terms: squid stir-fried with pineapple and onion
muc-ong-xao-dua-hanh-tay.image_alt: Squid stir-fried with pineapple, onion, scallions, and a light savory sauce.

ingredients.name: Cleaned squid tubes
ingredients.notes: Drain, lightly score the inside, and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Remove the eyes and tough core; cut into thin wedges.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into wedges.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use for marinating and final seasoning; adjust for saltiness.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For stir-frying.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Optional if the fish sauce is already strong.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use lightly.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; remove seeds for less heat.

preparation_steps: Rinse the squid briefly, drain, lightly score the inside, and cut into bite-size pieces.
Remove the pineapple eyes and tough core, then slice; cut the onion into wedges, slice the shallot, and cut the scallions.
Marinate the squid for 15 minutes with half of the fish sauce, seasoning powder, pepper, and half of the shallot.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the remaining shallot until fragrant. Add the squid and stir-fry over high heat for 2–3 minutes until just firm; transfer to a plate.
Stir-fry the pineapple and onion in the same pan for about 2 minutes, until hot and just softened.
Return the squid, add the remaining fish sauce, and toss for 1–2 minutes until just cooked.
Turn off the heat, add the scallions and chili if using, and serve promptly to keep the squid tender.
muc-ong-xao-dua-hanh-tay.serving_basis: A four-person dish for a Vietnamese family meal.
muc-ong-xao-dua-hanh-tay.time_note: About 45 minutes including preparation, resting, and cooking.

canh-hen-nau-khe-chua.name: Vietnamese Clam Soup with Sour Starfruit
canh-hen-nau-khe-chua.description: Sweet clams simmer with sour starfruit and tomato in a light broth finished with scallions and Vietnamese coriander. A bright, familiar soup for a rice meal.
canh-hen-nau-khe-chua.finished_dish: The broth is clear and gently sour; the clams are tender, starfruit slices remain distinct, and the herbs stay green.
canh-hen-nau-khe-chua.serving: Ladle into a large bowl and serve hot with steamed rice and a savory main dish.
tips: Boil clams just until the shells open, then let the cooking liquid settle and use the clear broth.
Add starfruit near the end to preserve its fresh sourness.
Season gradually because the clam broth may already be salty.
search_terms: Vietnamese clam soup with sour starfruit
canh-hen-nau-khe-chua.image_alt: A bowl of Vietnamese clam soup with sour starfruit, tomato, scallions, and Vietnamese coriander.

ingredients.name: Fresh clams in shell
ingredients.notes: Soak and rinse thoroughly; boil to open and reserve the clear cooking broth.

ingredients.name: Sour starfruit
ingredients.notes: Rinse, trim the firm ridges, and slice crosswise.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into wedges.

ingredients.name: Shallot

ingredients.name: Scallions

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander

ingredients.name: Cooking oil

ingredients.name: Water

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Add gradually after the soup boils.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the natural saltiness of the clams.

preparation_steps: Soak and rinse the clams thoroughly. Rinse and prepare the starfruit, tomato, shallot, scallions, and Vietnamese coriander.
Boil the clams until the shells open. Remove the meat and let the cooking liquid settle, then pour off the clear broth.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallot in oil, add the tomato and cook until softened; add the clam meat and stir briefly.
Pour in the clear clam broth and water, bring to a boil, and skim any foam.
Add the starfruit and simmer for 3–5 minutes until the broth is gently sour. Season with seasoning powder and salt.
Turn off the heat, add the scallions and Vietnamese coriander, and ladle into a serving bowl.
canh-hen-nau-khe-chua.serving_basis: A four-person dish for a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-hen-nau-khe-chua.time_note: About 50 minutes including preparation, resting, and cooking.

rau-den-xao-toi.name: Garlic Stir-Fried Amaranth Greens
rau-den-xao-toi.description: Amaranth greens are quickly cooked with fragrant garlic and light seasoning, keeping their natural sweetness and tender texture. A familiar plant-based side for a rice meal.
rau-den-xao-toi.finished_dish: The greens are just tender and vivid; the garlic is fragrant and the pan has little excess liquid.
rau-den-xao-toi.serving: Serve hot with rice and tofu or a vegetarian braise.
tips: Remove tough stems, rinse the greens well, and drain them before cooking.
Use only a little water and stir quickly to keep the greens bright.
A vegetarian seasoning powder may be used; check the label for a fully plant-based meal.
rau-den-xao-toi.image_alt: Green and red amaranth greens stir-fried with garlic until just tender.

ingredients.name: Amaranth greens
ingredients.notes: Remove wilted leaves and tough stems, rinse, drain, and cut into lengths.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use vegetable oil to sauté the garlic.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add a small amount to help the greens cook evenly.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly, then adjust.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Optional.

preparation_steps: Remove wilted leaves and tough stems. Rinse the greens several times, drain, and cut into serving lengths.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the garlic until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add the amaranth greens and stir quickly. Add the water, cover, and cook for 3–5 minutes until just tender.
Season with salt and stir for about 1 minute. Taste, turn off the heat, and add pepper if desired.

ga-hap-ngai-cuu.name: Steamed Chicken with Mugwort and Ginger
ga-hap-ngai-cuu.description: Lightly seasoned chicken is steamed with mugwort, ginger, and shallot. The meat stays moist and takes on a gentle herbal aroma for a family meal.
ga-hap-ngai-cuu.finished_dish: The chicken is fully cooked and tender, the mugwort is aromatic, and the steaming juices remain light.
ga-hap-ngai-cuu.serving: Cut into portions and serve warm with rice; lime, salt, and pepper may be offered alongside.
tips: Choose young mugwort leaves for a milder flavor.
Drain the chicken before seasoning and rub the seasoning over both the outside and inside.
Steam until the thickest part is fully cooked; adjust the time for the size of the chicken.
search_terms: chicken steamed with ginger and mugwort
ga-hap-ngai-cuu.image_alt: Vietnamese chicken steamed with mugwort, ginger, and shallot.

ingredients.name: Chicken
ingredients.notes: Clean, drain, and halve if needed to fit the steamer.

ingredients.name: Mugwort leaves
ingredients.notes: Pick young leaves and shoots, rinse, and drain.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice.

ingredients.name: Rice wine
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount to help clean the chicken; rinse if desired.

ingredients.name: Vinegar
ingredients.notes: Use a little with water to clean the chicken.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For seasoning the chicken.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Use lightly.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the chicken.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add to the steamer; do not pour directly over the chicken.

preparation_steps: Rinse the chicken, rub lightly with vinegar and a little salt, rinse again, and drain well.
Pick the young mugwort leaves and shoots, rinse, and drain; slice the ginger and shallot.
Mix the salt, seasoning powder, and pepper. Rub evenly over the chicken and rest for 10 minutes.
cooking_steps: Bring the steamer water to a boil. Line the steaming tray with some mugwort, ginger, and shallot; set the chicken on top and place a little mugwort inside if steaming it whole.
Arrange the remaining mugwort, ginger, and shallot around the chicken. Cover and steam for about 40–45 minutes, depending on size and whether it is halved.
Check that the thickest part is fully cooked; rest for 5 minutes, then cut into portions. Serve with the steaming juices and lime-salt-pepper dip if desired.
